newsitem.title: UK: Softs outlook - Buyers needed to boost weak prices.
newsitem.headline: Softs outlook - Buyers needed to boost weak prices.

text.p: Soft commodity markets are likely to rack up further losses this week, mainly due to an absence of buyers and a bearish technical outlook, traders said on Monday.
International currency movements should occupy players on the London cocoa market while robusta coffee will probably have to sink further before fresh buying interest emerges.
In white sugar, values should remain under pressure as physical offtake is limited but quality supply is strong.
Traders said the cocoa market would continue to watch the gyrations of sterling this week while the fundamental picture is mixed. The main snag seems to be a lack of industry buyers.
Speculative short covering would only boost the market to a limited extent as large-scale speculators would not bite below 975/980 stg basis March, they said.
Cocoa began a new uptrend last week as March pierced nearby resistance at 950 stg in a rally that was inspired by sterling's sharp fall against the dollar and mark.
Traders said industry buyers were unlikely to be deterred by the rally. "It's just purely a technical move and it will be difficult to sustain," said one.
But March held its position around 950 in a dull session on Friday and showed a marked inability to climb any further.
More concrete physical news is needed as traders were puzzled last week by a wide range of forecasts for the world 1996/97 cocoa deficit. The size of the crop in Ivory Coast also remained unclear.

Robusta coffee futures could see further retracement this week with no signs as yet of an abatement in fund selling, but traders did not rule out a technical bounce as a correction to the market's oversold condition.

The benchmark January contract tumbled some seven percent last week to touch a low of $1,309 on Friday and could easily break psychological support at $1,300, where fresh buying interest could emerge.
But origin sellers continued to mark up their prices last week although some were said to be under selling pressure.
Declining futures prompted some operators to turn to options to help protect their downside risks.
Physical coffee traders said Vietnamese sales could pick up as the main coffee region of Dak Lak recovered from its recent wet spell. But spot supplies still remain tight.
The outlook for white sugar futures remained bearish on a combination of solid European supply and weak technicals.
Traders said the spot March contract would face a tough task clawing back above $300 per tonne -- a key support level it tumbled through in a fierce New York-led selling bout last week.
"Now it's broken $300 I think it's going to struggle to get back up there. If New York has a sustained rally obviously it will do -- but I can only see the premium narrowing," said one.
The spot white/raw premium should again be a focus of attention this week as short funds in the raws will have to cover at some stage and possibly narrow March/March to $60.
"It (the arbitrage) will probably be a function of London staying reasonably pressured...and maybe New York rallying as we come into the start of the year," the trader said.

White sugar spreads remained flat and trading interest had been slight, leading some players to speculate whether buyers trying to cover non-urgent demand might delay until nearer the spot expiry in mid-February in the hope of even lower prices.
